newsitem.title: UK: Royal Sun ahead after after H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Royal Sun ahead after after H1 results.

text.p: Shares in newly merged Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group firmed in pre-market trading as results for the first half topped market forecasts, traders said.

The company reported pro forma interim results of 450 million stg for the first six months of the year after the completion of the merger of Royal Insurance and Sun Alliance to on July 19. Market expectations had ranged from 350 to 435 million stg.
The company declared an interim dividend of 6.5 pence
In early trading, Royal Sun shares added 5-1/2p to 417p.
"I think most forecasts were clustered between 365 and 400 million stg, so these figures are significantly better than expectations," said ABN AMRO Hoare Govett analyst Nick Bunker.

"The net asset value as pretty much what people had forecast -- most were around 400p and Royal did 403p. The shares will go better, but not dramatically prior to the analyst meeting. What people are looking for is more infoormation on the merger process itself," he said.
Executive deputy chairman Roger Taylor said the group had made rapid progress in integrating the two groups and was well on target to achieve its goal of full integration by 1998.
"It's a difficult situation at the moment but there's no doubt that, putting it simply, things are turning out generally better than most of us thought they would," he added.

While analyst forecasts look likely to be raised, Hurricane Fran, currently heading in the direction of North Carolina and expected to make landfall late Thursday may deter some from upping expectations before the impact of that becomes clear.

The company said the projected annualised expense reductions of at least 175 milllion stg were achievable by then and Royal Sun's much stronger distribution network and enhanced market positions in UK general and life business would be a better base for both leveraging international growth and reducing costs.
"The UK commercial lines account has been much better than I thought. Margins improved and it highlights the strength of the company in the commercial lines British arena," said Bunker.
"Canada has also improved quite dramatically continuing a theme we had with General Accident," he added.

Improvements in Canada Scandinavia and international division were offset by lower levels of profit in the UK and U.S. where the results were hit by the increase in weather related lossess in the first quarter of 1996.
In the first six months, worldwide weather related losses rose by 94 million stg. The insurance market remained generally soft, the company said.

"The big question for analysts going forwrad is whether the UK underwriting cycle is heading for a soft landing or not and whether we're going to see a bottoming out at acceptable levels in terms of results in 1997 and 1998," said Bunker.
